title: Petra and the Autopsy
premise: When a confession letter arrives at Yara Amberdale's morgue—postmarked the day after the funeral of the man it accuses—she realizes someone is confessing to a murder that officially never happened. The letter points to a drowning thirty years ago, ruled accidental, in which half of Petra Hollow's founding families were implicated. As Yara reopens the case, she discovers the town's most beloved citizens built their power on that buried night, and one of them will kill again to keep it there. The killer is the confessor's own child, who sent the letter to force the truth into the open; Yara closes the case by choosing justice over belonging, testifying against Petra Hollow's golden family and finally giving the drowned girl her name back.
about_author: Mara Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former rural journalist who spent a decade covering small-town courtrooms and county coroner elections. She writes mysteries about communities where everyone knows everyone—and no one says anything.

chapters.title: The Letter That Came Late
chapters.summary: Yara Amberdale's POV. A confession letter arrives postmarked the day after old-man Harrow's funeral, describing a drowning no one ever reported. Yara, who prides herself on closable cases, feels the first crack in her certainty. Emotional beat: unease disguised as professional curiosity.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Yara walks the cemetery cataloguing who attended Harrow's funeral and who didn't. She notices the Voss family plot has an unmarked grave from 1994. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: the weight of being the town's memory-keeper.

chapters.title: Petra Hollow Remembers Nothing
chapters.summary: Yara questions townsfolk and meets a wall of cheerful amnesia. The mayor, Delia Voss, warmly warns her off 'digging up gossip.' POV: Yara. Emotional beat: isolation—the first hint that belonging here is conditional.

chapters.title: The Drowned Girl
chapters.summary: In county archives Yara finds a 1994 file: seventeen-year-old Cass Merrow, ruled accidental drowning, signed off by Harrow himself. POV: Yara, with archival excerpts. Emotional beat: cold anger at how neatly the record was closed.

chapters.title: Tea with the Mayor
chapters.summary: Delia Voss hosts Yara for tea, offering help while revealing she knows exactly what Yara has found. POV: alternating Yara/Delia. Emotional beat: charm as a weapon; Yara feels both flattered and hunted.

chapters.title: The Confessor's Handwriting
chapters.summary: A graphologist friend dates the letter's ink and paper to decades ago—it was written in 1994 and mailed recently. Someone held this confession for thirty years. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: vertigo; the past isn't past, it's waiting.

chapters.title: Cass Had a Brother
chapters.summary: Yara tracks down Eli Merrow, Cass's brother, now a recluse outside town. He received a copy of the same letter last month. POV: Eli. Emotional beat: grief calcified into silence, beginning to thaw.

chapters.title: Alibis Woven Thirty Years Ago
chapters.summary: Yara maps the night of Cass's death: six teenagers at the quarry, each vouching for the others—including Harrow, Delia, and four now-powerful citizens. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: dread as the pattern of complicity emerges.

chapters.title: What the Quarry Gave Back
chapters.summary: A drought lowers the quarry water; divers find Cass's car—with damage inconsistent with the official story. POV: Yara and dive team. Emotional beat: grim vindication; the water kept the receipts.

chapters.title: Threats, Politely Worded
chapters.summary: Yara's office permit is suddenly 'under review'; her landlord gets a buyout offer. The pressure is legal, gentle, and unmistakable. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: Eli Breaks
chapters.summary: Eli admits he was at the quarry that night—he saw the others push Cass in and ran. He wrote the confession but couldn't mail it until now. POV: Eli. Emotional beat: shame finally spoken aloud.

chapters.title: The Second Letter
chapters.summary: An anonymous note threatens Eli by name, quoting words only the six could know. Someone inside the circle is protecting the secret actively. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: paranoia—who is watching whom?

chapters.title: Found Family
chapters.summary: Yara, Eli, and young deputy Rosa Okafor—an outsider like Yara once was—form an uneasy alliance over bad coffee and worse evidence. POV: Rosa. Emotional beat: warmth; belonging built on shared purpose rather than blood or history.

chapters.title: Harrow's Ledger
chapters.summary: Searching Harrow's estate, they find payments made annually to Cass's mother—hush money disguised as charity, authorized by all six families. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: disgust at corruption dressed as kindness.

chapters.title: One of Six Recants
chapters.summary: Former sheriff Tom Bricker, dying of cancer, confesses his part and names the ringleader: not Delia, but her late husband Marcus Voss—and someone still alive who finished what he started. POV: Bricker. Emotional beat: a coward's redemption, too late to be clean.

chapters.title: Rosa Is Silenced
chapters.summary: Rosa is suspended after planted evidence of misconduct; the machine turns its full weight on the alliance. POV: Rosa. Emotional beat: betrayal and heartbreak—the cost of belonging to the wrong side of town.

chapters.title: The Trap in the Archive
chapters.summary: Yara realizes the second letter-writer must have archive access. She baits a false record and watches who comes. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: hunter becoming hunter again.

chapters.title: The Confessor's Child
chapters.summary: The trap catches Delia Voss's son Julian—he mailed Eli's letter to detonate the secret he'd grown up inside. But Julian swears Delia wasn't at the quarry. POV: Julian. Emotional beat: a son's love weaponized into ruin.

chapters.title: Night at the Quarry
chapters.summary: Climax. The true keeper of the secret—Bricker's old deputy, now police chief Ada Renner—lures Yara and Eli to the quarry to finish thirty years of housekeeping. Julian's warning arrives just in time. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: terror, then resolve.

chapters.title: Confession, Recorded
chapters.summary: Renner, cornered by Rosa's hidden recorder and Julian's testimony, unravels: she pushed Cass, and the others buried it to save themselves. Arrests ripple through Petra Hollow's finest families. POV: Rosa. Emotional beat: catharsis—the machinery of power jammed by small stubborn people.

chapters.title: Naming Cass Merrow
chapters.summary: Yara presides over the exhumation and reburial, correcting the death certificate with her own hand. The town attends, some in shame, some in relief. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: mourning at last permitted.

chapters.title: A Coroner Who Closes Cases
chapters.summary: Epilogue. Yara keeps her job—or chooses to stay when she could leave—having learned that some cases close you instead. Eli plants a tree; Rosa is reinstated; Julian leaves town carrying his father's name and his mother's sentence. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: quiet peace; belonging earned, not inherited.
